evidence: Cic. Rep. 2.42 (Lewis & Short’s chapter): concentus ex distīnctīs sonīs
Cic. Rep. 1.27 (Lewis & Short’s chapter): distīnctōs dignitātis gradūs
terms.comment: The participle of distinguō: marked off, separate, each by itself; its other common sense is “adorned, set off with” (pōcula gemmīs distīncta, Cic.). The vowel before -nct- is long by the house rule; Lewis & Short leaves it unmarked.

evidence: Varr. in Non. 361.25: virtūtem propriam mortālibus fēcit (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Distinct in being one’s own and no one else’s (opposed to commūnis): proprium hujus generis, a feature peculiar to this kind.

terms.gloss: one thing and another; quite different things
terms.comment: Two things are distinct when one is aliud than the other: aliud est … aliud, “it is one thing to …, another to …” (see different).

phrases.latin: Aliud est fābula, aliud rēs gesta.
phrases.english: A story and a thing that really happened are quite distinct.

sources: Lewis & Short: distinguo · Lewis & Short: proprius · Lewis & Short: alius
